initial_context: Neutral assignment, actual proposed reader sources and sidecars, proposed reading-guide audience/path paragraphs. No target writer decisions, defenses or earlier verdicts read.
scope: Full proposed Chapters 1 and 2, including sidecar purpose/section summaries, eight figure captions and alt text; connected reading-guide audience and first-pass instructions.
initial_open_assessment: Chapter 1 separates represented values from neural activity and supplies count/covariance/attractor/diffusion meanings. Chapter 2 turns that geometry into a noise projection and distinguishes local from long-delay and mean-drift claims. This order supplies the assumptions needed by Chapter 3 without treating the three papers as one established circuit. The title changes mostly make those contributions explicit.

title_answers.title: Persistent neural activity can still accumulate memory error
title_answers.answer: Supported by the two-activity example: an along-family disturbance changes the angle from 5 to 6.5 degrees while activity stays on the fixed-point line. Can preserves the possibility rather than making all persistent activity fail.

title_answers.title: Patterns of firing rates represent a value
title_answers.answer: The tuning vector explicitly maps each represented angle to a rate pattern. The text distinguishes rate expectation from particular spike times and a neuron index from physical position.

title_answers.title: A variable spike count at a fixed rate
title_answers.answer: A fixed modeled rate gives a Poisson count with variable outcomes. The mean/variance formula and zero-count example establish the title directly.

title_answers.title: Mean squared displacement combines random spread with mean motion
title_answers.answer: The displayed identity adds displacement variance and squared mean displacement. Combines does not claim the unsquared mean is added. The preceding covariance/correlation identities support the later eye inference.

title_answers.title: Stable activity with a vulnerable stored value
title_answers.answer: The fixed-point and restoring/neutral definitions are followed by two disturbances that separate activity restoration from value restoration. The example is labeled a teaching model.

title_answers.title: Independent, unbiased changes give linear variance growth
title_answers.answer: Needs the fixed variance-per-time condition in its answer title. Independence and zero mean alone allow variance growth at other rates; see defect FM-TRUTH-01.

title_answers.title: A fixed spatial map differs from a value that wanders over time
title_answers.answer: The text distinguishes a random function drawn over locations from noise accumulating over time, while allowing visit-to-visit spikes to remain variable. It does not claim place-cell firing is deterministic.

title_answers.title: Spiking noise produces diffusion along the memory attractor
title_answers.answer: Supported within the explicitly tuned continuous-attractor, weak-fluctuation model. The chapter states the large-population and local-state limits and checks systematic drift separately.

title_answers.title: Recurrent spikes renew decaying synaptic activity
title_answers.answer: The jump/decay equation, summed input and transfer function show how recurrent spikes replenish decaying activation. Can in the opening correctly avoids claiming arbitrary recurrence suffices.

title_answers.title: The network's return flow determines the lasting memory change
title_answers.answer: The left zero vector removes decaying modes and preserves the tangent displacement. The tilted example demonstrates why return flow can differ from perpendicular projection.

title_answers.title: Projecting spike fluctuations gives the diffusion coefficient
title_answers.answer: The projected Brownian increment covariance gives 2D=sum(v_i squared r_i). The text limits the formula to local weak noise and does not equate high rate with greater damage under arbitrary retuning.

title_answers.title: Symmetric weights express diffusion through tuning curves
title_answers.answer: Under symmetric W, g prime is a left zero vector and normalization gives the displayed tuning formula. Stable-family and noise conditions remain explicit, with invertibility needed only when replacing input by the inverse transfer relation.

title_answers.title: Long delay errors depend on boundaries and local diffusion
title_answers.answer: The line/ring comparison and state-dependent moment equation show exactly how boundaries and local D alter delay errors. The title does not promise all state dependence curves the variance.

title_answers.title: A diffusion calculation does not determine systematic drift
title_answers.answer: The text explicitly separates variance growth from mean velocity and states why the leading noise projection does not determine exact noise-induced drift. Correlated-noise extension is kept distinct from a proved general information result.

title_answers.title: Figures distinguish memory motion from readout error and test diffusion
title_answers.answer: The figure account separates displacement of the latent coordinate from finite-spike readout uncertainty, and treats network simulations as model tests rather than direct animal measurements.

closed_fold_answers.title: Derivation: why a Poisson count has variance equal to its mean
closed_fold_answers.answer: The Poisson model, expected count and E[K]=Var(K)=lambda are visible before the fold. Later relative-error arithmetic and the concrete count example need that result, not factorial moments. The fold retains the exact moment calculation and introduces no visible dependent notation.

closed_fold_answers.title: Derivation: from random increments to the memory density equation
closed_fold_answers.answer: The visible path defines density, zero-drift Ito convention and initial point mass before the density equation, then gives its line/ring solutions and limiting error. Later state-dependent moments use the visible density equation and explicitly explain integration by parts. The folded test-function proof supplies its derivation without hiding a needed first definition or boundary assumption; conditions that remove boundary terms remain visible at line 328.

figure_caption_answers.answer: All four captions match their surrounding equations and illustrative status: Poisson rate SD falls from 20 to 4.47 Hz; attractor disturbances give 5 versus 6.5 degrees; bias and RMS scales meet at 0.40 degrees and 4 seconds; the paper map compares different questions without claiming one circuit.

All four captions match their surrounding examples: spike activation jumps by one and decays; a/lambda=1/2 maps the vertical jump of 2 to a lasting shift of 1; b=20 and tau=0.1 give D=100; constant-D angular reporting tends to pi squared over 3. The long-time figure stays outside the density-proof fold and is introduced and interpreted visibly.

cross_chapter_answers: Chapter 1 teaches conditional spike-generation independence without treating complete recurrent spike trains as independent; Chapter 2 repeats that distinction where correlated input would alter the projection.

The Chapter 1 fixed-point example explicitly defers tilted return flow to Chapter 2; Chapter 2 defines both zero vectors and demonstrates the missing perpendicular-projection correction before using it.

Both chapters use variance=2Dt for one coordinate under fixed D and appropriate boundaries. Chapter 2 distinguishes ring saturation, state-dependent diffusion and systematic drift; moving the density proof does not erase these limits.
Neither optional fold hides a figure, a first definition used by later visible prose, or the conditions needed to apply its displayed result.

defects.passage: ## Independent, unbiased changes give linear variance growth {#sec:FOUNDATIONS-DIFFUSION}
defects.literal_claim: Independent increments with mean zero give variance that grows linearly with elapsed time.
defects.likely_reader_inference: The two listed conditions are sufficient for the advertised result.
defects.failed_check: Necessary condition omitted from a result title.
defects.evidence: The following paragraph at line 161 also assumes every equal-duration increment has variance 2D Delta t with the same D. Only then does the displayed sum become 2D n Delta t.
defects.counterexample: Let independent increments have mean zero and variance j in equal-duration interval j. Their cumulative variance is n(n+1)/2, not linear in n. No research-source claim is needed for this direct variance identity.
prerequisites_checked: 01-foundations.md covariance sum rule and zero-mean MSD decomposition
01-foundations.md lines 159-181, including the fixed-D increment variance
defects.proposed_repair: Independent changes with fixed variance per time give linear variance growth
defects.sidecar_action: Match sec:FOUNDATIONS-DIFFUSION section_list title. Body already supplies the missing condition and does not need changing.

limits: No Stage 2 wording or Stage 3 reader-flow verdict is implied.

This scoped check did not revalidate every unchanged research finding against the original papers or inspect all image pixels. It read the equations and reader-facing caption connections, not a whole-book release.
verdict: One narrow heading condition needs repair; no other evidenced truth/reasoning defect found in the assigned changed reading path. Whole-book approval not given.
